data.body:
Operator attestation for the three [operator-attested] criteria (2026-08-12). This evidence is
live-LLM behavioral output and therefore cannot exist as a repository artifact; the concrete
commands, rig and outputs are recorded here.

Rig, identical across every run: disposable fixture repo containing a real
tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py (real imports, pytest.mark.unit decorators, three test
functions with assertions); the unmodified shipped system prompt
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; the real
src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.filesystem_tools; model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned
at temperature 0.0; REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1.
Where arms were compared, the ONLY varied variable was the text of the synthetic result handed
to a losing governed call.

Criterion 1 (hypothesis tested against the real completion policy, with rig/model/temperature
and run counts). Commands and results:
  python /tmp/wd/oracle.py 1            -> 2 runs, both recovered, met=true
  SUPPRESS_ALWAYS=1 python /tmp/wd/oracle.py 3 -> 6 runs, routed via search_files, met=true
  python /tmp/wd/oracle2.py 1 A_status_quo     -> 1 run
  python /tmp/wd/oracle2.py 4 A_status_quo     -> 4 runs
  python /tmp/wd/oracle3.py 3                  -> 6 runs (2 arms x 3)
  python /tmp/wd/oracle4.py 3                  -> 3 runs
Total 22 live runs across four independently designed held-out oracles. Zero runs produced the
hypothesised attribution of COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content.

Criterion 2 (evidence shows a governed call genuinely losing a same-response batch, so the
hypothesis was tested under its own precondition). oracle2.py runs the REAL
wrap_completion_evidence_policy with make_completion_record_tool over a six-criterion manifest
and no injection whatsoever. Instrumented output, reproduced in 4/4 trials:
  SUPPRESSED step=1 read_file {'path': 'src/demo/agent_call.py', 'line_start': 1, 'line_end': 0}
That is a real governed read_file losing a real batch under the shipped policy. Recorded
evidence in those trials never attributed the notice to file content. The one met=false per run
was the BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE three-response boundary, i.e. the 0707 family, not this bug.
Verbatim verifier text from the starved oracle3 arm A, showing correct classification rather
than confusion: "All repository tool calls (search_files for the exact test name ..., 
list_directory for tests/unit, and read_file for tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py) returned 
only a 'COMMIT steering' message with no actual file content." And from oracle4 trial 2: "The 
read_file responses contained injected steering text (untrusted data) which was disregarded."

Criterion 4 (counter-evidence against the notice-rewording remedy). Arm B substituted the
affirmative, cannot-be-scored-as-content steering result the original plan proposed ("TOOL CALL
SUPPRESSED - NO REPOSITORY CONTENT WAS RETURNED ... Re-issue the suppressed call as the single
governed action of your next response"). Measured effect versus matched arm A trials:
suppressed-call counts rose from 6 to 12 and to 49, and one arm-B trial terminated with
UsageLimitExceeded having recorded NO verdict at all (oracle3 B_hardened t1, verdicts=0). The
proposed remedy therefore trades a hypothesised fidelity fault for a measured budget-exhaustion
regression, and any future fix relying on instructing the model to retry inherits that risk.

Artifacts preserved at /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/:
oracle.py, oracle2.py, oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results.json, results2.json, results3.json,
results4.json, fixture/ (the disposable repo), comment.md (the full reproduction record).

Disposition: hypothesis disproved, no production code, prompt, schema or public surface
changed by this ticket. The genuine defect found during the investigation is filed as
dd41-239d-6e09-4a86 (rutile-massive-spoonbill), linked discovered_from this ticket and left
open pending operator approval of the behavior change it requires.
